summary: The 12-month Enrollment survey covers activity from July 1, 2022, through June 30, 2023, and is reported annually by eligible IPEDS postsecondary institutions, generally those participating in or eligible for Title IV federal student aid. Records are institution-level aggregates: enrollment tables count students once during the period, while instructional-activity tables report institutionally delivered credit or contact hours. The survey covers undergraduate and graduate enrollment, with some tables also including nondegree or high-school dual-enrollment populations; institutions and table populations must therefore be checked for the relevant enrollment level and status.

The Completions component covers awards granted and related program offerings by postsecondary institutions from July 1, 2022, through June 30, 2023. It reports aggregated counts or indicators at the institution level, with some tables adding program, award-level, demographic, or other dimensions rather than providing student-level records. The universe is institutions in the IPEDS reporting system with applicable awards or program offerings during the reporting period.

Fall Enrollment reports students enrolled at IPEDS institutions during the fall. Traditional academic calendars report enrollment as of October 15 or the institution’s official fall reporting date; institutions with program-specific or continuous-enrollment calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. Records are institution-level, with multiple records when enrollment is split by the table’s dimensions; optional components may not have data for every institution or year.

Finance is collected annually in the winter/spring collection window after the fiscal year closes; institutions report institution-level financial statements for their fiscal year, using the applicable GASB or FASB accounting basis. The universe is Title IV-participating postsecondary institutions in the IPEDS universe, with the finance form determined by institutional control and accounting standards. Across these tables, scholarship and fellowship amounts include source-specific discounts and allowances beginning in FY2020, while detailed functional and natural expenditure categories for fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are unavailable beginning in FY2016.

Graduation Rates is collected annually during the winter reporting period, with student outcomes reported as of August 31 of the survey year. It covers eligible degree-granting postsecondary institutions and full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohorts, with separate reporting rules for four-year, two-year, and less-than-two-year institutions. The survey measures cohort completion and transfer outcomes at specified percentages of normal time; it does not represent all enrolled students or all entering cohorts.

Human Resources data describe institution-level staff populations, usually measured from payroll as of November 1, with multiple records per institution; salary tables instead cover the academic year, and the new-hire table covers November 1, 2022 through October 31, 2023. Eligibility varies by table, with some files limited to degree-granting institutions having at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices. Where race/ethnicity and gender are collected, reporting has been mandatory annually since 2016, so the 2023 odd-numbered year has data.

This component covers the 2023-24 academic year and describes institutions and institution-related entities in the 2023-24 IPEDS universe; reporting is mandatory for institutions participating in Title IV federal financial aid programs. Most records are institution-level, while branch-campus and comparison-group files represent submitted subsets rather than a complete census of all possible locations or groups. The files combine institution-reported characteristics with some variables derived from other IPEDS collections, including admissions and financial-aid reporting.

These institution-level data cover student financial aid received during the academic year from July 1, 2022, through June 30, 2023. The survey applies to postsecondary institutions reporting undergraduate and/or graduate students eligible for the relevant financial-aid collections, with counts and dollar amounts reported by institution rather than individual student. Student populations and aid categories vary by table, so eligibility for a particular measure depends on enrollment level, attendance and degree-seeking status, and—in some cases—public-institution tuition residency.
